summary: Iteration 11 covered company orders, per-person orders, the header home button and the Sortiment favourites button. Backend: the new suite test_iter11_company_user_orders.py passes 14/14 and the iter10 regression passes 11/11. Test orders were inserted directly into Mongo, so no emails were sent. Frontend was tested at 375x667. (1) Company orders: Profil > Hantera kunder > Företag > company-row-patriks-bygg opens /admin/company?name=Patriks bygg. The segment shows 'PERSONER (2)' and 'ORDRAR (1)'. company-orders-list shows order-card-B10035 with company and email, and it expands with items and comment. (2) Per-person orders: the user page for test@hotmail.com shows 'Ordrar (1)', and user-orders-list contains order-card-B10035. (3) Home button: header-home-button (44x44) returns to the starting tab in every tested flow. Profil > users > company > user > home lands on /profile with no back button. Sortiment > heart > favorites > product > back > home lands on /shop. Hem > bell > notifications > order detail > home lands on /. Varukorg > bell > home lands on /cart. Profil > Mina ordrar > home lands on /profile. A cold deep link to /admin/user/<id> > home lands on /profile. There is no home button on /register or /forgot-password. (4) favorites-button sits next to notification-bell on both the gender picker and the product list, and favorites-count shows 1. Regression: the category dropdown, favourites rows and reorder (order detail > order-reorder-button > /cart with toast) all work. ONE NAVIGATION GAP: router.push('/(tabs)/...') from stack screens pushes a second (tabs) instance. After that, the home button leaves the old stack behind. No page errors. No deprecated Expo packages detected.

minor.issue: Orders are matched by current user_id membership OR the order's customer.company snapshot. If a user moves company, their old orders appear under both the new and the old company. This may be intended; please confirm.
An unknown user id returns 200 [] instead of 404. Harmless.

integration_issues.flow: Home button after jumping to a tab from a stack screen
integration_issues.issue: Stack screens call router.push('/(tabs)/cart') or push('/(tabs)/shop'). On expo-router 58 this pushes a NEW (tabs) instance onto the root stack: tab-profile appears twice in the DOM. Reproduced: Sortiment > heart > favorites > product > product-cart-button lands on /cart (2 tab bars). Then bell > notifications > home lands on /cart, but favorites-list and product-back-button are still mounted underneath. Browser/hardware back then goes to /product/11451648 instead of leaving the tab. The same happens after order detail > order-reorder-button. This partly defeats requirement 3 (go straight back to the tab without pressing back repeatedly). Affected: app/product/[id].tsx:87, app/order/[id].tsx:109, app/favorites.tsx:35, app/orders.tsx:34; probably also checkout.tsx:70,80 (router.replace('/(tabs)/shop')).

issues: It has no header-home-button (only back, heart and cart). For favorites > product it is only one level deep, so this is acceptable. Consider adding one for consistency.

action_items: Replace router.push('/(tabs)/cart' | '/(tabs)/shop') in stack screens (product/[id].tsx:87, order/[id].tsx:109, favorites.tsx:35, orders.tsx:34) with router.dismissTo('/(tabs)/cart') or the equivalent. This avoids stacking a second tabs navigator and keeps the home button and back behaviour clean. Also review checkout.tsx:70 and :80 (router.replace to '/(tabs)/shop').
Optional: confirm the intended semantics of company-orders when a user changes company (user_id OR customer.company snapshot).
critical_code_review_comments: navigation.ts: lastTab is module-level state, defaulting to '/(tabs)/profile'. After a cold deep link it returns to Profil, which is fine. It is not persisted, which is acceptable.
admin.py _company_rx: re.escape is used per word, so regex injection is safe ('.*' returns []). The match is anchored, so there are no partial matches.
company.tsx always fetches users and orders in parallel. That is fine, and the counts appear in the segment labels.

success_rate.frontend: 95% (all requested flows pass; one navigation gap with tab push)
